name: Revolution Medicines, Inc.

profile.description: Revolution Medicines, incorporated in 2014 and based in Redwood City, California, is a precision oncology company developing RAS(ON) inhibitors for RAS-addicted cancers. Its lead drug daraxonrasib (Rasonque) received FDA approval on August 26, 2026 for previously treated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial roughly doubled median overall survival versus chemotherapy (13.2 vs. 6.7 months). The pipeline also includes zoldonrasib (G12D), elironrasib (G12C), RMC-5127 (G12V) and RM-055, with Phase 3 trials in first-line and adjuvant pancreatic cancer and in lung cancer. Merck held acquisition talks valued at $28-32B in January 2026 that ended without agreement.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Revolution Medicines turned a first-in-class RAS(ON) inhibitor platform into an approved drug — daraxonrasib was approved August 26, 2026, about six and a half months ahead of its PDUFA date, after RASolute 302 showed median OS of 13.2 vs. 6.7 months (HR 0.40) and PFS of 7.2 vs. 3.6 months in previously treated metastatic PDAC [2][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): A multi-year collaboration with Iambic Therapeutics gives it access to the NeuralPLexer and PropANE AI models for discovery, but no AI-derived candidates or quantified results have been reported [4]. Market Share (2/2): It is defining the RAS(ON) inhibitor category in pancreatic cancer — the Expanded Access Program alone distributed daraxonrasib for more than 2,000 patients across nearly all U.S. states before approval [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Specific programs and timelines are disclosed — RASolve 301 (NSCLC) enrollment completing 2026 with readout in 2027, RASolute 303/304/305/309 in PDAC, RASolve 307 (elironrasib, first-line G12C NSCLC) starting Q4 2026, RMC-5127 data in 2027 and RM-055 entering the clinic in Q4 2026 [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Q2 2026 R&D was $394.9M and FY2026 opex is guided to $2.1-2.2B, far above peers of its size [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): The company's purpose — revolutionizing treatment for patients with RAS-addicted cancers — is specific, ties directly to an unmet need in one of the deadliest cancers, and has shaped a decade of structure-based drug discovery around a target long considered undruggable [4][6]. Community Impact (1/2): Before approval it opened an FDA-cleared Expanded Access Program and within weeks was supplying daraxonrasib for 2,000+ patients, a concrete patient-access commitment, though no charitable foundation or dollar-quantified giving was found [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found; headcount growth drove higher R&D and G&A [1]. Insider Buying (0/2): The last open-market purchases were by director Thilo Schroeder in December 2024 at $46; in September-October 2026 the Chief Development Officer, General Counsel, a director and another officer all sold shares at $187-207 — net selling [5].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanical score (Growth sleeve). Revenue was $0 in FY2024-FY2025 and Rasonque launched only in late August 2026, so revenue growth, 5yr revenue CAGR and profit margin are not meaningful and are excluded; PEG is unavailable — leaving D/E (1x), ROE (2x) and forward P/E (1x), 4 weight units. Liquidity floor passed: 1.92M avg shares x $188.17 = ~$361M/day [6]. D/E 45.7% -> 1.00; ROE -79.1% -> 0.00 (x2); forward P/E -32.6 (negative) -> 0.00 [6]. Weighted sum 1.0 / 4 = 2.5 -> 3 (rounded half up). Balance sheet liquidity is strong — $3.94B of cash and securities at June 30, 2026 after $2.225B of April equity and convertible financing and $250M from Royalty Pharma, with up to $1.5B more available — but Q2 net loss was $644.4M [1].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9 — IMMUNE): Revolution Medicines sells a patent-protected, FDA-approved small-molecule cancer drug whose value rests on Phase 3 survival data and regulatory exclusivity — AI cannot substitute for an approved therapy, and no analyst commentary flags AI disruption risk [2][3]. AI is an enabler, not a threat: the Iambic collaboration applies AI structure prediction to hard-to-drug oncology targets, though third-party analysis notes the approach is unproven and shared model rights limit exclusivity [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Revolution Medicines shows the makings of an infinite player: a cause (defeating RAS-addicted cancers) that has guided a decade of science, the courage to stay independent and build its own commercial organization rather than accept a reported $28-32B Merck bid, and a pre-approval access program for 2,000+ patients. It is still young — the cause has not yet been tested through leadership succession or a commercial downturn — and insider selling plus heavy reliance on capital markets keep it in MIXED territory.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The company exists to outmaneuver RAS-driven cancers, a target long called undruggable, and its strategic choices — RAS(ON) platform, multiple mutant-selective inhibitors, adjuvant and first-line trials — trace directly to that cause [1][4]. It is genuine and partially lived, but at roughly a decade old it has not been validated across leadership transitions or multiple cycles.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Management let Merck acquisition talks valued at $28-32B end without a deal in January 2026 over valuation, choosing to launch daraxonrasib itself, then raised $2.225B and built global commercial capabilities [7][1]. It also opened an expanded access program before approval and is spending $2.1-2.2B in 2026 opex on a broad Phase 3 program — costly long-term bets made consistently [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership has been stable, with Mark Goldsmith serving as CEO and chairman through the company's evolution from venture-backed startup to commercial-stage company [4]. No independent culture or retention evidence was found, and rapid headcount growth for the launch is a test still underway [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has evolved from early RAS companion inhibitors to the RAS(ON) inhibitor platform, absorbed EQRx (whose warrants it still carries), and is now transitioning from a research organization to a commercial one [1][6]. These are significant adaptations within its cause, not a reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors' strengths or framing rivalry as a source of learning; communications focus on the company's own data and timelines [1].

investment_thesis: Revolution Medicines now owns an approved, first-in-class therapy in one of oncology's largest unmet needs: Rasonque (daraxonrasib) roughly doubled median overall survival (13.2 vs. 6.7 months, HR 0.40) in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer and was approved with Breakthrough, Orphan and Priority Review designations about six and a half months early [2][3]. With $3.94B of cash, Breakthrough designation in non-G12C KRAS NSCLC, first-line and adjuvant PDAC Phase 3s, an NSCLC readout due in 2027, and a pipeline of mutant-selective inhibitors, the company has multiple label-expansion paths, and Merck's reported $28-32B interest highlights strategic value [1][7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and execution: at about $40B market cap the stock already exceeds Merck's reported $28-32B talks range, yet the company has had no product revenue until the late-August launch, posted a $644.4M Q2 net loss (including a $151.0M warrant charge), and guides $2.1-2.2B of 2026 opex [1][6][7]. Infrastructure scores just 3 on ROE of -79% and a negative forward P/E, the label carries warnings for GI perforation, interstitial lung disease and skin toxicity, and insiders have been net sellers at $187-207 [3][5][6].
key_catalysts: U.S. launch trajectory of Rasonque in second-line metastatic PDAC following the August 26, 2026 approval, with Q3 2026 results the first quarter of commercial sales [3]
RASolve 301 daraxonrasib NSCLC readout expected in 2027 (Breakthrough Therapy in non-G12C KRAS NSCLC) and RASolve 307 elironrasib first-line G12C NSCLC start in Q4 2026 [1]

First-line (RASolute 303, 305) and adjuvant (RASolute 304) pancreatic cancer trials, plus EMA phased review under the Cancer Medicines Pathfinder project, that could multiply the addressable population [1]
key_risks: Commercial execution — first-ever launch with FY2026 opex of $2.1-2.2B; slow uptake could require more capital beyond the $3.94B cash and Royalty Pharma facility [1]

Safety and competition — label warnings for GI perforation, interstitial lung disease, stomatitis and dermatologic toxicity, and rival KRAS programs from large pharma could limit share in lung and colorectal settings [3]
Valuation risk — a ~$40B market cap already above Merck's reported $28-32B deal range leaves little room for trial setbacks such as a miss in RASolve 301 or first-line PDAC [6][7]
